comments.text: ​​ @aksarairl if you have overheating issues try undervolting and maybe limit the frequency of the processor so it does not reach turbo. I do this on all of my systems, they lose maybe 5% of CPU performance but they never go above 75c which makes the system last longer in theory.
comments.author: @voidvoid5151

comments.text: @voidvoid5151 oh yes, I’ve done that and maximum processing units to 99 to ensure that doesn’t happen, but I think since I’ve been using 10 hours everyday  the thermal paste is dried up. But I’ll try it out, if you have a video or an article to do that, do link it here! Thanks
comments.author: @aksarairl

comments.text: ​​ @aksarairl I'm using Linux with the cpupower utility to set the maximal frequency and CPU governor. It has lots of options as it's an AMD CPU. As for repasting it should be easy to do, it might take 1-2 hours to take everything apart, disconnect the battery, cleaning the dust from fans etc., removing the old thermal paste with ear cleaning sticks and repasting and putting everything together. I didn't do it so far for this device since I really had no thermal issues but I did it on an older RoG and it reduced temps by 20c at least.
comments.author: @voidvoid5151

comments.text: ​ @aksarairl I'd also recommend buying some decent Noctua or CoolerMaster or Artic paste, they might be a bit expensive for what it is but they are worth the money, you can use it on multiple devices and they last way longer than manufacturer thermal paste.
comments.author: @voidvoid5151

comments.text:
I bought a Philips Evnia monitor with 260Hz but returned it due to its not so good viewing angle.
Does this monitor have good viewing angle like any IPS? I mean the color don't turn into this silvery shadow if you changed the angle..
comments.author: @MohOEM

comments.text:
As far as I know, no. 

I have this right opposite to my window, so light directly shines on it and  it's still good, not as good as OLED, but definitely no color changes and perfectly usable. 

People who have seen the monitor in person have also appreciated the colors.

comments.text: Any OSD menu preview?
comments.author: @DotaSpy-l8z

comments.text:
It’s regular Lenovo OSD, so I didn’t include it, but if you want I can publish it as shorts for you to check it out. 

Plus the Lenovo artery software lets you control the monitor settings (basically a mirror of OSD) through a software, so I didn’t see why one would use that. 

But compared to the Lenovo legion Y27qf-30 pro, it’s much harder to move around settings mainly due to the buttons. The pro model has a joystick and makes it breeze to fly through settings.
comments.author: @aksarairl

comments.text: SO i've been hearing that this monitor has some issues such as buzzing noise aka coil noise or pixle bleeding , How's your experience with this monitor so far for both productivity , offline gaming and online gaming . I'm thinking about buying this as my main
comments.author: @Zirael.bussiness

comments.text:
As far as the buzzing noise goes, I hear it only when the monitor goes on standby mode which isn't a big deal for me as my power settings doesn't let it go to standby mode. 

In terms of the experience, I have the more expensive sibling which is the Lenovo Legion Y27qf-30 Pro and I like this one better. I use it for all sorts - A lot Gaming, Video editing, Color Grading, and of course work as well, it's been flawless and since I'm from Ireland, we don't have a lot of options here. This seem to be the best and I don't regret it. 

Tip : If you have a students account, just wait for a sale and you can grab it at a good price. I bought this monitor for around €180.
comments.author: @aksarairl
